reviews.review:
This game is pretty unique. In a good and in a bad way. The game is an incremental in a sense that you have to just do your thing and watch the numbers go up and make a lot of money. However, it has so many systems on top of each other, each quite difficult at times to keep tabs on what is the best way to do your choices. There is definitely chances to go super deep and make your own spreadsheets, but it's enjoyable with not going too deep either. 

Early game is interesting but can easily break your run if you screw it up.
Mid-game is slightly grindy, but it's so short it didn't bother me.
Late game is interesting and you can definitely do a lot of strategic choices that feel genuinely different.

The UI definitely needs some QoL updates, but it works for what it is. I also had a few minor performance issues with the probe in the end game (it sorta hitches) and the filters (they kinda hitch too), but that might just be my 10 year old gaming rig.

Just to add: I played this quite extensively during playtest and the playtime numbers up there don't really reflect how much time I've used on this game.
